title: Generalize custom element upgrade concept by allowing `customElements.define(name, Subclass)`

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

labels.name: topic: custom elements
labels.description: Relates to custom elements (as defined in DOM and HTML)

body:
Currently, custom elements start off as `HTMLElement` and if registered, are later upgraded to the class they are registered with in `customElements.define()`.
This can only be called once for each element name; even calling `customElements.define()` again with exactly the same arguments throws (!)

```js
class MyElement extends HTMLElement {}
customElements.define("foo-bar", MyElement)
customElements.define("foo-bar", MyElement)
// NotSupportedError: Failed to execute 'define' on 'CustomElementRegistry': the name "foo-bar" has already been used with this registry
```

This causes unnecessary error conditions and prevents certain defensive definition patterns. 

This proposes to relax this rule, and allow calling `customElements.define()` multiple times with the same name, as long as the new constructor is either the same as the existing constructor (`A === B`) OR a subclass of the existing constructor (`A.prototype instanceof B`). 

Since it would be a subclass, nothing needs to be undone, and it is simply a generalization of going from `HTMLElement` to custom element constructor, and it solves a lot of nice **use cases**.

- This would allow for progressively enhanced custom elements, where **longer definitions can be deferred** while render-critical aspects could be loaded early. 
- It would also allow the current pattern of **subclass factories as mixins to be applied post-hoc**, without requiring the entire chain to be specified in advance.
- Another use case is **automatically fetching element definitions**: register all known elements with their base class, then whenever a tag is first encountered, fetch its definition
- But the main driver is that it paves the way for **declarative custom elements that can be enhanced later with JS** without re-specifying the entire element, without introducing complex new concepts such as "pending custom element", and without monkey-patching: the HTML syntax can simply generate a constructor for the declarative definition, and authors can enhance that at any time by subclassing.
